headline: supply_any_transactions (Tx.lean): sum of balances = totalSupply holds, and the contract still holds its code, after ANY finite list of transactions run by EthLib's processTransaction, whoever sends them and whatever they call at any depth (calls back into PEPE, creations, failed and reverted calls included), from a block state where it holds. Assumptions: the six 'Transaction theorems' lines of `assumptions`; limits: the 'Transaction level' lines of `not_covered`.

claims.supply_message_any_depth: one call run by EthLib's processMessage, to any account and any code, at any depth: 'C holds the code of PEPE and the invariant holds' is kept, with or without an error. Fork from Berlin. Assumes Seq.Sane (a call that runs at C runs CODE), Seq.Good at the start, Seq.Clean of this run.
claims.supply_transaction: one whole transaction run by EthLib's processTransaction (gas purchase, EIP-7702 authorizations, the message, refunds, fee, deletion of accounts): block state before to block state after. Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam. Assumes Seq.TxClean of this transaction and Seq.Good at the start.
claims.supply_any_transactions: the same after any finite list of transactions (Seq.Chain), each at its own fork and block environment.
claims.supply_from_zero: the same from the base case shape: C holds the code and every storage word of C is zero (inv_zeroBase). This is NOT the real deployment state of PEPE (the constructor mints the supply).
claims.transfer_closed: Sanity/Closed.lean (the ten-token audit, PEPE-1 and PEPE-3; hand-written). ONE closed instance of the hypotheses of the supply theorems, at message level. wState: one account at the mainnet address of PEPE that holds the code of PEPE, owner (slot 0) = address 2, balance of Witness.CALLER1 = 5, totalSupply (slot 3) = 5, all else 0. m_w: transfer(2, 1) from Witness.CALLER1, no value, gas limit 1000000. Statement, for Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam and every block and transaction environment: Seq.Good holds in wState (the account holds the code and the invariant holds: good_wState, inv_wState); EthLib's processMessage ends m_w with no error and output true; at the end the caller has 4, the address 2 has 1, totalSupply is 5; the run meets Seq.Clean with Q := SepMsg (the run-local hypothesis of supply_message_any_depth); and Seq.Good holds in the end state by supply_message_any_depth. Hypotheses that stay, both about keccak and NOT proved: hA : Sep W_KEYS with W_KEYS = [CALLER1W, 2, 1], and hH : hashOf CODE != EMPTY_CODE_HASH. So the hypotheses are shown consistent with a real successful run only relative to these two; Sep itself is not shown satisfiable.
claims.older_model_kept: Seq.lean (inv_calls, process_step, calls_process): top-level messages only, where every other step is ASSUMED to keep the storage of C (Untouched). Kept because other files use it; the theorems of Tx.lean do not use that assumption.

assumptions: Transaction theorems (supply_transaction, supply_any_transactions, supply_from_zero), run-local hypothesis Seq.TxClean.call / .create with Q := SepMsg: every message that really enters the code at C during this transaction satisfies Sep (callKeys m) (keccak separation for its caller and first two argument words, NOT proved), and every code that a creation of this transaction really deposits, when it has the keccak hash of the code of PEPE, is that code (no keccak collision on these codes, NOT proved). Nothing is assumed about messages or codes outside the run. supply_message_any_depth assumes the same as Seq.Clean of its run.

Transaction theorems, Seq.TxClean.auths: no EIP-7702 authorization of the transaction sets a code (0 or 23 bytes) with the keccak hash of the code of PEPE (4517 bytes). Only a keccak collision breaks it; NOT proved.
Transaction theorems, Seq.TxClean.data: the call data of a transaction sent to C is below 2^256 bytes.
Transaction theorems, fork range: each transaction has Fork.dencun <= fork < Fork.glamsterdam (supply_transaction, the cons of Seq.Chain). supply_message_any_depth: Fork.berlin <= fork.

Transaction theorems, start state: Seq.Good C CODE (Inv C) on the block state before the first transaction: C holds the code of PEPE (its code hash is keccak256 of the code and not the empty hash) and the invariant holds (supply_any_transactions, supply_transaction); supply_from_zero assumes Seq.HoldsCode and all-zero storage of C instead.

Transaction theorems, supply_message_any_depth only: Seq.Sane C CODE message (if the top message runs at C, it is a call that runs the code of PEPE with call data below 2^256 bytes). The transaction theorems prove this from HoldsCode.

Sep W_KEYS (hA of inv_wState, good_wState, transfer_closed; Sanity/Closed.lean), W_KEYS = [CALLER1W, 2, 1]: Sep for the three words of the witness call. It is the smallest named list the frame theorems let through and unfolds to 33 keccak facts, each over all 2^160 address words: slot 3 is the balance slot of no address (1); no other address has the balance slot of each of the three words (3); the 9 allowance slots keyed by two of the words are no balance slot and not slot 3 (18); the 3 blacklist slots are no balance slot and not slot 3 (6); slots 0, 6, 7, 8, 9 are no balance slot (5). inv_wState uses three of them only (uniqueness of the balance slot of CALLER1W; slots 0 and 3 are no balance slot). None can be proved in this model: keccak has no proved property and 2^160 inputs cannot be computed by the kernel. No instance of Sep is proved anywhere.

hH : hashOf CODE != EMPTY_CODE_HASH (holdsCode_wState, good_wState, transfer_closed): the keccak hash of the code of PEPE is not the hash of the empty code. True (Test/Hash.lean computes the hash at build time with #eval) but not proved in the kernel: the kernel computation of keccak over the whole code ran a box out of memory in an earlier round (WBTC), so it was not tried again.

Sep (callKeys message): a hypothesis about keccak only, NOT proved. For the caller and the first two argument words (each masked to 160 bits): slot 3 is no balance slot; their balance slots are the balance slot of no other address; allowance slots keyed by two of them and their blacklist slots are no balance slot and not slot 3; slots 0, 6, 7, 8, 9 are no balance slot. Used by the supply invariant, the sequence theorems and the readable corollaries of the 13 functions that touch mappings. Not used by the path theorems, ok_<fn>, the Sanity witnesses, or the readable corollaries of blacklist, setRule, transferOwnership, renounceOwnership.
message.data.size < 2^256 (hsize') in every completeness and later theorem.
Fork: from Berlin for paths, completeness, invariant, readable and sanity; from Paris for the lift to top-level messages and sequences.

Gas and upper fork bound (the ten-token audit, PEPE-7, fix 7): the one-counter meter (Evm fork Nat). The generated frame theorems (paths, ok_<fn>, supply_<fn>, readable, Sanity/Zero) and the per-message theorems of Seq.lean carry only Fork.berlin <= fork (Paris for the per-message lift) and no upper bound in their statement. They are true as stated at every such fork, because they speak about EthLib's frame runner instantiated with the Nat meter; but EthLib's processTransaction uses that meter only below Glamsterdam, so they describe the real chain only for fork < Glamsterdam. The link to the chain is made in Tx.lean, where supply_transaction and Seq.Chain state Fork.dencun <= fork < Fork.glamsterdam, and in Sanity/Closed.lean, where transfer_closed states fork < Fork.glamsterdam. The generator was not changed to add the bound to the older theorems: it is a file of the shared kit, the bound would be an unused hypothesis in each of them, and every other token would have to be regenerated. The EIP-8037 two-counter meter is not ported.
The start state is 'At CODE message 0 [] .empty gas state substate evm': a fresh frame at pc 0 with empty stack and memory.
Sequence lift: message.code = CODE, the target is no precompile, and for a successful call no value is moved (process_value_fails shows a call with value fails).
supply_preserved and the sequence theorems assume the invariant in the start state; the constructor is not verified.
statement_form: Upstream's Gas.simulated set lacks SHL, SHR, SLT, SGT and XOR, which optimized code uses (PEPE: 78 SHL, 8 SLT). So paths are stated over EthLib's Logic.SpecG / HoareG (the real step function), and completeness and every later family over 'EndsL runChild evm s := exists within, Evm.runFrame (step fork) (step_decreases fork) bound runChild evm within = .ok s' for every bound and every message runner (TokenKit/Evm/SafeL.lean). This is EthLib's real frame runner, not a weaker model. It is not upstream's 'Ends fork' predicate, so the PEPE statements do not have literally the same shape as SHIB's.
not_covered: name() and symbol(): only 'no storage write, no log' for every successful run (Loops.ro_name, Loops.ro_symbol) and the entry paths. That a call of name() or symbol() CAN end with no error is not witnessed (no success path theorem, no output, no gas, no Sanity witness), so ro_name and ro_symbol could hold for no run at all (the ten-token audit, PEPE-4); supply_name and supply_symbol are sound either way. The exact return data (the string) is not proved: the optimized string copy has two nested loop shapes (storage to memory, then memory to return buffer) and was not attempted beyond read-only.
The EIP-8037 two-counter gas meter (by the brief).
The readable corollaries state requirements, storage, output and logs; they do not restate gas (the path theorems give the exact gas).

Sanity witnesses exist for the 32 success paths only. The 133 revert and 22 stuck paths have no witness; the generator drops paths with contradictory conditions but a remaining revert path is not shown non-empty.

Sanity witnesses run in a state with a single account (the contract) and from one fixed caller (Witness.CALLER1). In Sanity/Zero.lean the account has no code in the state (the code comes from the message) and the storage does not meet the invariant; Sanity/Closed.lean has the one witness where the account holds the code and the invariant holds.

Paths that need the caller word 0 (transfer_p3, approve_p3, transferFrom_p12, p18, p26, p33, p39, increaseAllowance_p4, decreaseAllowance_p4, burn_p2): they exist in the model, which does not exclude a caller with address 0, but no signed transaction reaches them. For the same reason a statement about what can happen after renounceOwnership is an argument about real senders, not a theorem: in the model a caller with address 0 passes the owner check when slot 0 is 0 (the ten-token audit, PEPE-9).

No single 'no mint' theorem (the ten-token audit, PEPE-8): there is no statement 'totalSupply after <= totalSupply before for every successful call' as WBT has (total_le). The claim is read off the 20 readable corollaries and ro_name / ro_symbol; for blacklist it also needs the keccak fact Sep.black (its corollary takes no Sep and so does not itself say slot 3 is kept). The kit generator gen_nomint.py is written for the storage layout of WBT and was not adapted.

Seq.TxClean and Seq.Chain have no closed instance: it would need a concrete signed transaction run through processTransaction (signature recovery, fee and balance checks), which is not built here. The closed instance of Sanity/Closed.lean is at the level of one message (processMessage).
supply_valueSent, supply_short, supply_other do not exist: these three have no successful run and supply_preserved covers them.
The constructor and the deployed storage values are not verified; nothing is proved about the real chain state.
Transaction level: what a block does between transactions is not linked (withdrawals, the system calls of EIP-4788, 2935, 7002, 7251, rewards). Seq.Chain strings transactions only.

Transaction level: forks before Dencun. There the end of a transaction can delete an account that ran SELFDESTRUCT, and it is not proved here that the code of PEPE never runs it (the library tracks instead that C is not created in the transaction and not marked for deletion, which EIP-6780 gives from Dencun).
Transaction level: Glamsterdam and later (two-counter gas meter).
Transaction level: the base case of supply_from_zero is all-zero storage; the constructor run that leaves the real start state is not linked.
ETHERSCAN_KEY was not set: the work is from the bytes and the ABI; names of storage variables follow the ABI getters.

contract_findings: Every function is non-payable: any call with value reverts.
The ABI decoder reverts on short call data and on dirty address or bool argument words (high bits set).
transfer / transferFrom succeed only if neither from nor to is blacklisted.
While uniswapV2Pair is 0, a transfer succeeds only if from or to is the owner (trading closed).

When uniswapV2Pair is set, limited is on and from is the pair (a buy), the new balance of to must be within [minHoldingAmount, maxHoldingAmount]. The holding limits are buy-side only: they apply only when from = pair and limited is on, and only to the balance of the receiver. Wallet to wallet transfers and sells to the pair are never limited (the ten-token audit, PEPE-11).

transferFrom checks the blacklist of from and to, NOT of the spender (the caller): a blacklisted spender can still move tokens of others with an allowance. approve, increaseAllowance and decreaseAllowance have no blacklist check at all (the ten-token audit, PEPE-11).
setRule with min > max makes every buy from the pair revert while limited is on; blacklist(pair, true) blocks every transfer to or from the pair.

burn(amount) goes through the same hook with to = address 0: it needs blacklists[0] = 0 and blacklists[caller] = 0, and while the pair is 0 it needs caller = owner or owner = 0. So the owner can block every burn by blacklisting address 0.

If the owner renounces while uniswapV2Pair is still 0, every transfer between non-zero addresses fails and no transaction can change it (no signed sender is the owner 0, so setRule cannot be called), and only burns pass. This is an argument about real senders, not a theorem: see the caller 0 line of not_covered.
transferFrom moves the balances first and checks the allowance after; the allowance is always decreased (no infinite allowance case) and an Approval log follows the Transfer log.

Owner powers: setRule(limited, pair, max, min) writes slots 6, 9, 7, 8 with no bound or check on the values, at any time (the pair can be changed or set back to 0, which closes trading again); blacklist(account, flag) for any address, the pair included, with no log; transferOwnership (new owner not 0); renounceOwnership.

No function mints: no success path raises totalSupply (read from the 32 success paths and the readable corollaries; not one theorem, see not_covered). burn lowers totalSupply and the caller's balance by the same amount.
No external call, no delegatecall, no selfdestruct in the code.
